subject: science
skillName: Designing a Device That Changes Energy Forms
intro: Many devices change energy from one form into another. A hand-crank flashlight changes the energy of your motion into electrical energy and then into light. A rubber-band car changes the stored energy of a stretched rubber band into energy of motion. A solar cell changes light energy into electrical energy. Engineers design such devices, test them to see how well they work, and then refine them, making changes to improve how much energy they convert or how well they do the job.

items.prompt: A hand-crank flashlight lights up when you turn the crank. Describe the energy changes from your hand to the light.

steps: Turning the crank uses the energy of motion from your hand.
Inside, that motion is changed into electrical energy.
The electrical energy is then changed into light energy at the bulb.
solution.answer: Motion energy from your hand changes into electrical energy, which changes into light.

items.prompt: A student builds a rubber-band car. What energy change makes it move, and how could the student test it?

steps: Winding the rubber band stores energy in the stretched band.
When released, that stored energy changes into energy of motion, moving the car.
The student could test it by releasing the car and measuring how far it travels.
solution.answer: The stored energy of the stretched rubber band changes into motion; test by measuring how far the car goes.

items.prompt: A solar-powered toy stops in the shade but runs in sunlight. What energy conversion does it use?

steps: The toy needs light to run, so light must be its energy source.
A solar cell changes light energy into electrical energy.
That electrical energy runs the toy, which is why it only works in the light.
solution.answer: It uses a solar cell to change light energy into electrical energy, so it runs only in the light.

items.prompt: Name the three steps engineers use when making a device that converts energy.

steps: They design the device, test it, and then refine (improve) it.

items.prompt: A rubber-band car does not roll very far. Suggest one change to refine it and explain the expected result.

steps: Refining means making a change to improve the device.
Winding the rubber band more stores more energy, or using lighter wheels wastes less energy.
Either change would let more stored energy become motion, so the car should roll farther.
solution.answer: Wind the rubber band more or use lighter wheels; more stored energy becomes motion, so the car rolls farther.

items.prompt: Why is testing an important step when building an energy-converting device?

steps: A new design might not work as well as hoped.
Testing shows how well the device converts energy and where it fails.
The results tell the engineer what to refine to make it work better.
solution.answer: Testing shows how well the device works and what to improve, guiding the refining step.
